chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, Blessed and Exalted, on the Day he meets Him, like an idol worshipper.

key_terms.مُدْمِنُ: Habitual drinker / one who makes a habit of

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a habitual wine drinker on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni uses this hadith to illustrate the concept of *tadim* (habituation), where the repetitive nature of the sin transforms the drinker's spiritual state to resemble that of a polytheist (*mushrik*) who worships idols. This comparison underscores the severity of wine consumption in Shia jurisprudence, suggesting that while not technically *kufr* in doctrine, it leads to a similar degree of spiritual alienation from God. The imagery of 'meeting God' emphasizes the eschatological consequence of this habitual state.
